title: Euler and the Seven Bridges of Königsberg (1736)
explainer: Many of the graph algorithms in this lesson trace back to a single 1736 puzzle: could a walker cross each of Königsberg's seven bridges exactly once and return to the start? Leonhard Euler answered no by stripping away irrelevant geometric detail and reducing the city to landmasses and bridges - vertices and edges - the same abstraction every graph algorithm here relies on. His proof is usually credited as the founding result of graph theory.
